correctness.rationale: For every pointed nonempty finite E-structure and \(k\ge0\), \(\ell\ge2\), the two pumping operations preserve the entire equality/E atomic diagram set on \(k\) witnesses and \(\ell\) universally assigned variables. If neither exists, at most \(k\) witnesses, \(k(\ell-1)\) other marked-class points, and \((\ell-1)^2\) free-class points remain. The explicit three \(\ell\)-variable prohibitions attain \(k\ell+(\ell-1)^2\). Every \(n\ge k+\ell\) follows by universal-downward preservation or single-point pumping. An enumerator independently checks 1,655 pointed finite cases; it does not substitute for the proof.

value.rationale: The optimal two-parameter polynomial ceiling gives a reusable exact stopping bound for finite spectra in a natural semantic first-order fragment. The theorem explains two distinct independent nonpumping obstructions (size and number of E-classes) and saturates both with explicit extremal models. This is stronger and more informative than the coarse graph Ramsey upper bound and does not hinge on arbitrary small numerical experiments.
